headlines.title: ‘I have a lot to live for': Greg Papa opens up about cancer fight, family and job
headlines.description: In his own words. Greg Papa sat down with NBC Bay Area for his first television interview since recent health complications from his cancer diagnosis. NBC Bay Area’s Raj Mathai met with the legendary broadcaster at his home in Marin County for a wide-ranging interview that focused on facing death, family, being laid off by KNBR and more. “I do not want to die,” Papa said. “I’m going to fight as hard as I can, fight to stay alive. I have a lot to live for.” For decades, Papa’s voice has brought to life some of the most colorful sports moments. He’s given the Bay Area memories that span generations from his time covering the A’s and Raiders to the Warriors, Giants and 49ers. These days, his voice is strong and still resonates, but the game has changed. Doctors diagnosed him with leukemia last summer. He got sick while vacationing in France. “There were many nights there that I felt, you know, I may die,” Papa said. “Cancer is unfair. Cancer is sudden. Cancer is cruel.” His lifeline turned out to be his bloodline. His younger sister, Judy, was a perfect match. In March, she donated her stem cells for a bone marrow transplant. A month later, things took a turn for the worse. Complications from the transplant caused pneumonia, and his lungs collapsed. He nearly died and spent 78 days in the ICU. “I was put on a ventilator,” Papa said. “I was intubated. I was in an induced coma for about five days. It went from a life-threatening situation for certain to a life-altering one…I’ve made a lot of progress since I’ve been home. I made a lot progress since late July.” He continues his fight and wants to get back to what he loves in the radio booth. “I’m cleared, by the way, to go back on the radio show that I had that I no longer have,” he said. In early August, Papa was laid off by KNBR. In his first public comments since the layoff, he said, “I was fully preparing to return to work. There was never discussion that that would not be the case. And then one day you get a phone call and I thought it was a return-to-work plan…I was cleared, my hematologist cleared me [for the radio show] and they went the other way and they chose to terminate my contract.” Cumulus Media, which owns KNBR, issued a statement on Aug. 7 acknowledging Papa’s departure, writing, “our respect and gratitude for everything Greg has given to KNBR, its listeners, and its team runs deep. We are continuing to explore ways we can bring his voice back to the station, and we wish Greg strength, healing, and a full recovery.” Papa still has his job as the San Francisco 49ers radio announcer. He said he’d like to come back sometime this season to call games, but he didn’t know if that was possible. The David Benzer Strike Out Fear Foundation has set up a GoFund Me campaign to help with the financial burden of Papa’s long recovery.
headlines.source: Raj Mathai, Christine Ni and Alex Bozovic

headlines.title: 2028 MLB All-Star Game coming to San Francisco's Oracle Park
headlines.description: The 2028 MLB All-Star Game will be played in San Francisco’s Oracle Park, adding another major sporting event to the Bay Area’s calendar. The San Francisco Giants and Mayor Daniel Lurie’s office confirmed the game is scheduled for July 12. “With its passionate fanbase, world-class ballpark, and rich baseball history, San Francisco will be an outstanding host for All-Star Week, which culminates in one of Major League Baseball’s best traditions, the Midsummer Classic,” MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred said in a statement. “We look forward to bringing the excitement of All-Star Week and the celebration of baseball to the Bay Area.” The last time the All-Star Game was played at the Giants’ ballpark was in 2007. The announcement comes amid a busy stretch for Bay Area sports, with the region also hosting Super Bowl LX, the 2025 NBA All-Star Game and the FIFA World Cup 2026. Lurie celebrated the announcement on social media, pointing to the city’s focus on public safety and clean streets. “We’ve made public safety our top priority since day one, and we’re delivering safe and clean streets for residents and visitors,” Lurie said. “Now, people want to be here again.” MLB 9 hours ago Jackson Flora Aug 12 Mike Krukow Aug 11 The Giants will host the Midsummer Classic for a fourth time overall after Candlestick Park held the first All-Star Game of the 1961 season and also baseball’s summer showcase in 1984. Oracle Park is set to become the eighth active ballpark to hold the All-Star Game multiple times, joining Fenway Park in 1946, 1961 and 1999, Wrigley Field (1947, 1962, 1990), Angel Stadium (1967, 1989, 2010), Dodger Stadium (1980, 2022), Progressive Field (1997, 2019), Coors Field (1998, 2021) and T-Mobile Park (2001, 2023). Giants President and CEO Larry Baer said the club is “incredibly honored” and expressed his gratitude. “This is a tremendous opportunity to showcase our organization, our city, and the incredible passion of our fans on baseball’s biggest summer stage,” he said in a statement. “Hosting the All-Star Game is more than celebrating the game’s brightest stars, it’s a chance to highlight the people, neighborhoods, and culture that make our community so special. Few cities offer the unique combination of sports, culture, innovation, entertainment, and natural beauty that defines San Francisco. We look forward to welcoming players, families, fans, and visitors from around the world for a week that will create lasting memories and have a meaningful impact throughout our region.”
headlines.source: NBC Bay Area staff and The Associated Press

headlines.title: DA seeks adult charges for teen accused in Fairfield graduation shooting
headlines.description: A minor charged with killing a young man after his high school graduation ceremony in Fairfield may be tried as an adult following a petition from the Solano County District Attorney’s Office. On Tuesday, 17-year-old Khare Clark appeared in juvenile court to plead not guilty to charges of murder and several counts of attempted murder in the shooting death of 18-year-old Jamario Baker. On June 3, Clark allegedly opened fire in the parking lot of Sem Yeto High School following the school’s graduation ceremony. An 11-year-old and two adults were also injured in the shooting. Around 1,000 people attended the ceremony, according to the district attorney’s office. Clark was arrested in Texas in July following a monthlong investigation and was extradited to California for trial. A hearing date to transfer Clark to adult court will be set at a proceeding scheduled in September. According to the district attorney’s office, Clark will be transferred to adult court “if and only if” it is decided he will not be rehabilitated if placed under the authority of juvenile court.

headlines.title: New housing development opens in East San Jose
headlines.description: A new housing development aimed at helping working families afford homes in the Bay Area has opened in East San Jose. City and community leaders celebrated the opening of The Kirk, an 18-home, single-family housing development. The community includes two below-market-rate homes for qualified buyers, as well as tax incentives for first-time homebuyers. San Jose Mayor Matt Mahan said the development is part of a broader effort to address the city’s affordable housing crisis. The homes are 100% electric and solar-ready.

headlines.title: 32-year-old woman killed in solo crash in Walnut Creek
headlines.description: A 32-year-old woman died in a solo vehicle crash in Walnut Creek early Thursday morning, according to police. The crash was reported at 5:06 a.m. in the area of Rossmoor Parkway and Stanley Dollar Drive in the Rossmoor retirement community, Walnut Creek police said. The woman, the lone occupant in the vehicle, was pronounced dead at the scene and her name was not yet being released as of Friday. The crash remains under investigation. Anyone with information is asked to call Walnut Creek police at 925-943-5844.

headlines.title: Former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao faces new allegations in federal case
headlines.description: Former Oakland Mayor Sheng Thao was back in court Friday morning as she faces new allegations in what prosecutors are calling a “pay-to-play” scheme involving Thao, her boyfriend and a pair of Oakland businessmen. Thao declined to comment as she entered the federal courthouse Friday morning with her lawyers for a pretrial motion hearing. Attorneys for Thao and her co-defendants asked the chief judge of the U.S. District Court to throw out some evidence before the trial. They argue the evidence is “prejudicial” and includes material that is not relevant or predates the alleged conspiracy. The federal case includes accusations of bribery and fraud, as well as new allegations stemming from a 2023 trip to Vietnam funded by co-defendants Andy and David Duong, who own California Waste Solutions. According to an affidavit filed with the court, a reporter began asking questions about alleged misconduct during the trip. Prosecutors say Thao became upset and concerned about how a news story about the allegations could affect her political future. Prosecutors allege Thao pressured Andy and David Duong into paying a reporter’s associate $10,000 to prevent the negative story from being published. The case also includes allegations that one of the California Waste Solutions owners kept dozens of secret recordings, photos and videos of politicians in compromising positions. Lawyers argue that the defendants should not be treated as a group when the court decides whether individual pieces of evidence, including audio and video recordings, can be used. Oakland Jul 30 Oakland Feb 6, 2025 Oakland Jan 27, 2025 Prosecutors said they do not intend to use some of the recordings from the 2023 Vietnam trip. However, they said many of the pieces of evidence the defense wants excluded are relevant because they show a pattern of cooperation and conspiracy among the co-defendants and their financial entanglements. The judge said she will review each disputed piece of evidence individually and rule on what will be allowed in the coming days. The trial is scheduled to begin Oct. 19, and the government has already identified 68 witnesses. The judge’s rulings on the disputed evidence could affect that witness list and what those witnesses will be allowed to testify about.

headlines.title: Pedestrian taken to hospital after being struck by driver in San Jose
headlines.description: A pedestrian was taken to a hospital in critical condition Thursday night after being struck by a driver in San Jose, according to police. The collision happened at about 10:12 p.m. in the area of Thornwood Drive and Blossom Hill Road, not far from Westfield Oakridge mall, according to police. The driver stayed at the scene and cooperated with investigators, police said. An investigation is underway. Additional information wasn’t immediately available.

headlines.title: Redwood City liquor store manager started deadly fire at business, police say
headlines.description: A Redwood City liquor store manager who died in a fire at the business last year intentionally started the blaze, which also killed another person, according to police. The fire broke out inside Avenue Liquors on Roosevelt Avenue last November. Benigno Nuguid Pare, 56, and Anil Kumar Sharma, 25, were found dead in a loft area near the back of the business, police said. Investigators smelled gasoline in the area. Police said Pare was found with a chain around his wrists, secured by a lock. Additional examination revealed the chain was tightly secured around one of his wrists but loose on the other. “Based on the physical evidence, witness statements, surveillance video, and the totality of the investigation, investigators believe Pare intentionally introduced and ignited gasoline in the loft area,” police said in a statement. Police also said the store’s front and rear exits were locked from the inside. A motive remains unknown. headlines.title: Timber Fire in Big Sur grows to 4,545 acres amid tough conditions
headlines.description: The Timber Fire near Big Sur continues to grow and had spread to 4,545 acres as of Friday morning while firefighters continue to battle the massive blaze amid tough conditions, according to Cal Fire. The wildfire remains 7% contained, Cal Fire said in an update around 6:35 a.m. The fire has prompted evacuations and the closure of a stretch of state Highway 1 in Monterey County, from mile marker 45.1 near Big Sur Bakery to mile marker 37 at Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park Vista Point. The fire has crossed Longwood Creek and reached Olmstead Mountain, according to authorities. There have been no reported injuries as of Friday morning, but more than 500 structures are threatened, according to Cal Fire. A heavy marine layer has helped slow the fire’s spread, while crews continue building containment lines behind homes on the east side of the freeway. They have faced difficult conditions in steep drainages, and fog has severely limited aircraft support, according to Cal Fire. All evacuation orders and warnings remain in place. The Monterey County Sheriff’s Office issued orders for zones MRY-F023, MRY-F025, MRY-F026, MRY-F027 and MRY-F028-A, and warnings for zones MRY-F021-B, MRY-F022, MRY-F024, MRY-F028-B and MRY-F029. An emergency evacuation shelter remains open at Carmel Middle School, 4380 Carmel Valley Road in Carmel. The SPCA for Monterey County is providing a dedicated area and support for evacuees with pets.

headlines.title: Experts say the East Bay's Hayward Fault is ‘overdue' for a major earthquake
headlines.description: Thursday’s earthquake along the Hayward Fault served as a reminder of how “the big one” could impact populated spots in the East Bay. The Hayward Fault produced a 3.8 magnitude earthquake, but experts say it’s capable of producing a major one, too. “We do have historical records happening of earthquakes happening roughly every 150 years or so, and if you do the math, we are definitely a little bit overdue for an earthquake on the Hayward Fault based on those previous historical earthquakes,” Angie Lux with the UC Berkeley Seismology Lab said. The folks at the UC Berkeley Seismology Lab say the Hayward Fault is capable of producing a magnitude 6.0 or 7.0 quake. The Hayward Fault actually runs under the seismology lab as well as Cal Memorial Stadium and the Greek Theater. It also stretches through San Jose, Fremont, San Leandro, Hayward, Oakland, El Cerrito and Richmond. Alyssa Goard has the full report in the video above.

headlines.title: 1 dead after car drives off cliff in Santa Cruz, lands in ocean
headlines.description: One person died and another was injured after they drove off a cliff in Santa Cruz and landed in the ocean early Thursday morning, according to officials. The crash happened at about 12:50 a.m. off West Cliff Drive near the Steamer Lane surfing spot, officials said. One person was able to get out of the car on their own and reach safety, according to officials. They suffered minor injuries. Rescue swimmers jumped into the ocean and were able to pull a second person from the submerged car. Despite life-saving measures, that person later died at the hospital, officials said. Officials did not immediately say who was driving the car when the crash occurred. The cause of the crash is under investigation.

headlines.title: 3.8 magnitude earthquake, multiple aftershocks strike near San Leandro
headlines.description: A 3.8 magnitude earthquake struck near San Leandro Thursday morning, according to the United States Geological Survey. The quake hit at 8:30 a.m. and was centered 2.4 miles north of San Leandro, 4.9 miles north-northwest of Ashland and 5.3 miles south-southwest of Moraga, the USGS said. “It was just like a big jolt,” Alicia Battle of Castro Valley said. “We had a few things knocked over – nothing damaged – but it was pretty strong.” The initial quake was followed by 3.0 and 2.8 magnitude aftershocks at about 9:07 a.m., according to the USGS. No damage was immediately reported. “This is not something unexpected for the Bay Area, especially for this region,” said Dr. Angie Lux, a project scientist for Earthquake Early Warning at the Berkeley Seismology Lab. “It doesn’t mean that we are going to have a big earthquake soon, but we do know at the same time that we are overdue for a large earthquake on the Hayward Fault.” Following the initial earthquake, BART temporarily held trains before allowing them to run at reduced speeds while crews completed safety inspections of the tracks. Normal BART service later resumed, but the agency said there were major residual delays systemwide.
